page.layout: One page of text, one column. Running head and page number at the top. Heading "CONCIO XXVIII." with the subtitle "Prouerb. 21." Then an italic epigraph beside a woodcut initial, then the body text. Signature mark at the foot left. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: Aliter dicunt: Melius est scire simplicia,
communia ac vera, quàm subtilia & falsa, vel
cum opinione. Item dicunt: Melius est mo-
dicum didicisse de rebus diuinis, quàm multa
de creaturis. Nos possumus & illud addere:
Melius esse Christum Dominum (qui est pa-
nis viuus qui de coelo descendit) in ecclesia
discere & gustare, quàm omnes artes & di-
sciplinas, quae in scholis & academijs docen-
tur, scire, omnesque libros de philosophia,
humanis legibus, historijs gentium devora-
re. In Christo enim sunt omnes thesauri sa-
pientiae (quae pacifica est) ac scientiae recon-
diti, Colos. 2. Iacob. 3. Qui ad hunc venit, nō
esuriet: & qui credit in eum, non sitiet vn-
quam, Ioan. 6. Ipsi sit honor & gloria in ae-
ternum, Amen.
CONCIO XXVIII.
Prouerb. 21.

page.notes: The large woodcut initial is read as M, forming "Melius"; the letter is partly hidden, so it is marked [?]. A small mark stands in the left margin beside "esuriet", with no note text. The signature "M 2" is partly unclear; the numeral is marked [?]. The text ends mid-sentence at the foot of the page and continues on the next page.
